title: Sale Ad Creatives With Editable Offers | AIVideosUGC
description: Build a sale ad creative from one product photo. Add the confirmed price, code and end date after download, then reuse the scene when the promotion changes.
lead: Build the product scene now, and add the confirmed price, code, and end date after you download.

faq.q: Will the discount be printed on the image for me?
faq.a: No. Keep the percent, the price, the code, and the end date as text you add after download, so you can check every character.

faq.q: Can I reuse the scene for the next promotion?
faq.a: Yes. The product scene is separate from the offer. Replace the text when the promotion changes and keep the same visual.

faq.q: Can I show the old price next to the sale price?
faq.a: Only if you actually charged that old price. Check the comparison-pricing rules where you sell before you publish the claim.

faq.q: Can I add a countdown to the sale video?
faq.a: No. The clip does not include a timer. Add it in your editor or ad platform after download, where you control the end time.

faq.q: How many credits does a sale photo or video use?
faq.a: A photo uses 24 credits. Video uses 24 credits for 6 seconds, 40 for 10, 60 for 15, or 120 for 30. The cost shows before you start, and a failed job returns those credits.

faq.q: Do I need a creator for the sale scene?
faq.a: No. Start from your product photo. If a person appears, that person is generated, not a real customer.

faq.q: Can I run the file as a paid sale ad?
faq.a: Yes. The download has no AIVideosUGC watermark. The platform's ad rules still apply.

faq.q: Can I make sale visuals for many products at once?
faq.a: No. Each product photo is its own job. Start the next product when you are ready.

faq.q: How much empty space should I leave for the offer?
faq.a: Leave clear room for the offer line and the code without covering the product. Check the smallest screen you will use and make sure both stay readable.

benefits_h2: Discount ad images with room for the price

benefits.t: Start before the offer is final
benefits.d: Build the product scene while the price and the code are still being decided. Leave the product clear, with empty space for the offer.
benefits.alt: Denim jacket on a hanger against a pale wall with open space for an offer.

benefits.t: Keep the scene when the code changes
benefits.d: Swap the price, the code, or the end date in your editor and leave the product scene as it is. A late change does not send you back to a shoot.
benefits.alt: Adult hands fold a checked picnic blanket beside a basket at a park table.

benefits.t: Get a square post or a short clip
benefits.d: The photo is square. A clip from the same photo runs 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds, in 9:16, 1:1, 16:9, 4:3, or 3:4.
benefits.alt: Adult hand places a wireless charging pad on a dark desk.

benefits.t: Make the scene from the photo you have

reviews.h2: How shops make a sale banner for an online store
reviews.lead: Three ways a shop leaves room for an offer that is not final yet.

items.t: Leave open space beside the jar
items.d: They upload the jar and ask for a clean counter with empty room on one side. The percent off is typed later, so a changed number does not need a new scene.

items.t: Run the jacket scene again next week
items.d: They reuse the same jacket scene for the next code. Only the offer line in the editor changes.

items.t: Fold the blanket, then add the end date
items.d: They show the blanket in use and leave the end date out of the picture. The date is added after download, once the sale window is real.

trust.h2: What you still edit after download
trust.lead: The offer is yours to type, and the file is yours to run.

items.t: The price stays out of the generated scene
items.d: Percent, price, code, and end date are typed by you after download, so you can proofread every character.

items.t: A commercial file with no watermark
items.d: The download has no AIVideosUGC watermark. You can use it in paid promotions, subject to platform rules.

items.t: The credit cost before you start
items.d: A photo uses 24 credits. Video uses 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits for 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds.

items.t: Credits back if the job fails
items.d: A failed job returns its credits automatically. A finished file is not refunded just because you dislike it.

items.t: The upload stays in your account
items.d: The product photo and the result stay in your account. They are not published until you share them.
Add a track you have rights to, and any captions, in your editor. They are not generated into the file.
